solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Random strikes around newly-constructed NI dams

indicators.note: the word for strikes is placed around the rebuilt letters, holding them inside

parts.note: strikes as a noun are hits

indicators.note: something newly constructed has been put together afresh, so these letters are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: Random explosions hit freshly built dams in Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'newly-constructed' is the rearrangement signal for NI DAMS; 'around' wraps the word for strikes about the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hit-or-miss is haphazard, succeeding only by chance, so it is a fair synonym for random.

clue.text: Ring after noon and attempt to engage a public official

indicators.note: the ring letter is placed after the letter for noon

parts.note: a ring is round, the shape of the letter O

indicators.note: to engage something is to take it in, so the word for attempt holds the A

parts.note: an attempt is a try

explanation.surface: Someone phones after midday hoping to hire a functionary.
explanation.definitionFit: A notary is a legal officer who witnesses documents, a kind of public official.

clue.text: What restaurants in Tokyo do as a memento?

definitions.meaning: Japanese restaurants stock (keep) the rice wine sake, read as two words, four and four
a memento is an object kept as a reminder of someone or something

explanation.surface: A question asking what Japanese eateries do, doubling as a souvenir.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as KEEP SAKE: Tokyo restaurants keep the rice wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A keepsake is a small item kept in memory of a person or occasion, a memento.

clue.text: Imprisonment of the Parisian on ship

parts.note: du is French for 'of the', as a Parisian would say
re means on or concerning
SS is the abbreviation for steamship

explanation.surface: A Frenchman held captive aboard a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Duress in law includes unlawful restraint or confinement, so imprisonment is a recognised dictionary sense.

clue.text: Upset Italian girl locking up a liqueur

indicators.note: locking up means holding inside, so the combined letters enclose the A
upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the short form of Italian is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Maria is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A distressed Italian woman shuts away a glass of liqueur.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'Upset' means turned upside down; 'locking up' has the combined letters enclose the A.
explanation.definitionFit: Tia Maria is a brand of coffee-flavoured liqueur from Jamaica.

clue.text: Waterloo Station's architect

indicators.note: the 's stands for has: the words have the name within them

explanation.surface: Asking who designed the London railway terminus at Waterloo.
explanation.walkthrough: The name runs across 'WaterLOO Station'. Waterloo is a London rail terminus.
explanation.definitionFit: Adolf Loos was a Czech-born Austrian modernist architect famous for rejecting ornament.

clue.text: Circle deadheaded rose, thorny

parts.note: to circle is to spin round

indicators.note: deadheading a flower removes its head, so the first letter of the flower's name goes

parts.note: taken as written, the flower

explanation.surface: A gardener walks round a spent rose bush that pricks.
explanation.definitionFit: Spinose is a botanical term meaning covered with spines, the same as prickly.

clue.text: Back crazy supporting acts in vaudeville

parts.note: to back a proposal is to second it
bananas is slang for crazy

explanation.surface: Supporting mad warm-up turns in a variety show.
explanation.definitionFit: In American vaudeville the second banana was the comic's stooge, the performer in a supporting role.

clue.text: Orderly's codeword

definitions.meaning: orderly here means regular, all the same, consistent
in the NATO phonetic alphabet the letter U has its own codeword used in radio talk

explanation.surface: The password used by a hospital orderly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Orderly' tempts as a hospital attendant, which would fit the clothing sense; here it is an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Uniform as an adjective means consistent and regular, and it is also the radio code for the letter U.

clue.text: Married lady's worried about son in old soap

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go about, around, the letter for son
worried means agitated, so these letters are churned into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, part of the anagram fodder
here the 's counts as a letter of the fodder

explanation.surface: A wife is anxious about her boy in a long-running drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' is the rearrangement signal and 'about' wraps the result round the son. Mrs Dale's Diary was a BBC radio soap of the 1940s to 1960s.
explanation.definitionFit: Mrs Dale's Diary was a long-running British radio serial, an early soap opera.

clue.text: Bar, place abroad stocking soft fruit

indicators.note: stocking means keeping in stock, holding inside
abroad here means all over the place, scattered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, part of the anagram fodder
taken as written, part of the anagram fodder
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, soft

explanation.surface: A pub somewhere overseas sells soft fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abroad' rearranges BAR PLACE into CRABAPLE, which stocks the P.
explanation.definitionFit: A crab apple is a small sour wild apple, a type of fruit.

clue.text: Grandma's sculpture?

definitions.meaning: Grandma here is the American folk painter known by that nickname, and this is her surname
Michelangelo carved a famous marble statue of the Hebrew prophet for a papal tomb

explanation.surface: Asking whether a statue was carved by the grandmother.
explanation.definitionFit: Grandma Moses was a celebrated folk artist, and Michelangelo's Moses is a renowned statue in Rome.

clue.text: Oceanic bird's occasional visit to New York

indicators.note: a visit to a place means going into it, so the word goes inside

parts.note: odd can mean occasional, as in the odd visit

explanation.surface: A seabird drops in on New York now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: The noddy is a tropical tern found over warm seas, so an ocean bird.

clue.text: Film of a lake in European country

indicators.note: the A and the lake letter sit in the country's name

parts.note: Austria is a country in central Europe
L is an abbreviation for lake, as on maps

explanation.surface: A movie shot beside a lake somewhere in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film' looks like the start of a description; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Australia is a 2008 Baz Luhrmann film starring Nicole Kidman and Hugh Jackman.

clue.text: Disrespect shown over international symbol of freedom

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece is shown over, above, the second

parts.note: taking a liberty is an act of disrespect
a cap is awarded for playing for one's country, so an international player is a cap

explanation.surface: Contempt displayed toward a cross-border body or emblem of liberty.
explanation.walkthrough: A cap is the honour, and the player, in British sport for appearing in an international match.
explanation.definitionFit: The liberty cap, or Phrygian cap, was worn by freed Roman slaves and became an emblem of revolutionary liberty.

clue.text: Body of troops ordered to carry equipment

indicators.note: to carry here is to hold within, so the word for ordered encloses the equipment

parts.note: bade is a past tense of bid, meaning ordered
rig is equipment or gear

explanation.surface: Soldiers are instructed to bear their kit.
explanation.definitionFit: A brigade is a military formation of several battalions, a large body of soldiers.

clue.text: Cinerama developed in US

definitions.note: the definition is a noun used attributively, as in US goods

indicators.note: developed suggests film processing, but here it means worked into another form, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: The widescreen Cinerama process was devised in the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed' hints at film processing, fitting Cinerama, but signals rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: American and US are interchangeable adjectives for things of the United States.

clue.text: Novelist and daughter ahead of disorderly crowd

indicators.note: the daughter letter comes ahead of, before, the crowd

parts.note: a rabble is a disorderly crowd

explanation.surface: A writer and her girl walk in front of an unruly mob.
explanation.definitionFit: Margaret Drabble is an English novelist, author of The Millstone among others.

clue.text: Infantryman's son after money

indicators.note: the son's word is placed after the word for money

parts.note: dough is slang for money
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A foot soldier's boy is chasing cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places the son's word after the money one.
explanation.definitionFit: Doughboy was the informal name for an American infantryman in the First World War.

clue.text: A fortune's blown exposing vampire

indicators.note: a fortune blown is squandered and scattered, so these letters are dispersed into a new order

parts.note: here the 's counts as a letter of the fodder

explanation.surface: Wasting a fortune reveals someone who lives off others' blood.
explanation.definitionFit: Nosferatu is the vampire count of the 1922 German silent film, and a byword for a vampire.

clue.text: Perception shown by university in a large town

indicators.note: the university letter goes in the rest

parts.note: a city is a large town

explanation.surface: Insight displayed by a university in a big town.
explanation.definitionFit: Acuity is sharpness of perception or mind, keen discernment.

clue.text: King's ambassador and staff

parts.note: HE stands for His Excellency, the title of an ambassador
a staff is a rod

explanation.surface: A monarch's envoy and his attendants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' looks like employees, but it is a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: Herod the Great was the king of Judaea in the Gospel nativity story.

clue.text: Healthy drinking it, a mineral

indicators.note: drinking takes something in, so the word for healthy swallows the other word

parts.note: hale means healthy, as in hale and hearty

explanation.surface: A fit person sips some mineral water.
explanation.definitionFit: Halite is rock salt, the naturally occurring mineral form of sodium chloride.

clue.text: A symbol of fertility in the outskirts of Nairobi?

parts.note: the outermost letters of Nairobi are ..., and the phrase spelt out in words makes the bull's name

explanation.surface: A fertility emblem found on the edges of Kenya's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Spell out the outer letters as words, 'N and I'. Nandi is also a Kenyan people, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Nandi is the sacred bull of the Hindu god Shiva, associated with fertility.

clue.text: Ten falling into trap immediately after

indicators.note: falling into a trap means ending up inside it

parts.note: a net is a trap
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: Ten creatures tumble into a snare one after another.
explanation.definitionFit: Next means following straight on, coming directly after in order.

clue.text: Paul and Hayley, mostly, organised a festival

indicators.note: organised means arranged, so the letters are put into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, part of the anagram fodder

indicators.note: mostly means all but a little, so the name loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written before its last letter goes

explanation.surface: Two people, Paul and Hayley, arranged a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts HAYLEY to HAYLE; 'organised' then rearranges PAUL HAYLE. Up Helly Aa is a Viking fire festival held in Lerwick, Shetland.
explanation.definitionFit: Up Helly Aa is an annual Shetland fire festival in which a Viking galley is burnt.

clue.text: Small surviving navigational instrument

parts.note: extant means still existing, surviving

explanation.surface: A tiny old sea-going device that has lasted to this day.
explanation.definitionFit: A sextant measures the angle of a star or the sun above the horizon to fix a ship's position.

clue.text: Doorkeeper flying to Syria

indicators.note: flying suggests letters scattered through the air, so they come down in a new order

explanation.surface: A porter is taking a flight to Syria.
explanation.definitionFit: An ostiary is a church doorkeeper, once one of the minor orders of clergy.
